scenes.title: UWA C72 Centrifuge Service Bay
scenes.institution: National Geotechnical Centrifuge Facility — C72 bay
scenes.reference_notes: Actual C72 installation and close view inspected: teal tapered central pedestal, upright front drive motor, pale horizontal arm and hanging bucket on one end, paired cylindrical counterweight stacks on the opposite end, upper service platform and square ceiling access opening. Local machine bay is visible, not a measured room plan. C61 and C72 images on the same website are different machines and must not be fused. Current wall dimensions and hidden drive internals are unknown.
observed_cues: Teal tapering central support with arched openings
White cantilever arm and hanging bucket contrasted with metal counterweight stacks
Square ceiling service opening above grated access platform

equipment.role: Position the bounded beam azimuth and hanging basket attitude around a retained dry calibration block.
equipment.evidence: Original geometry derived from inspected official apparatus photos; unreported details estimated

support.evidence: Continuous authored support to the laboratory floor; basin recessed below the floor datum where applicable

task.description: Position the bounded beam azimuth and hanging basket attitude around a retained dry calibration block.

scenes.title: UTS Infrastructure Robotics Test Bay
scenes.reference_notes: Official panorama inspected: recessed concrete water tank occupies the left foreground, metal guard rail bounds its edge, yellow overhead bridge crane sits on blue steel girders, and tool drawers, assembly benches and inspection fixtures occupy the right and rear work area. Panorama distortion prevents metric floorplan recovery. Exact robot models and fixtures are not identifiable at this resolution; do not invent a specific deployed robot from adjacent page text. Source states a 45 kL tank but no verified dimensions.

Yellow crane supported by blue columns and runway beams
Wall-side benches and drawers around a clear central access area

scenes.title: UNSW WRL Segmented Wave-Paddle Bay
scenes.institution: Water Research Laboratory — segmented wave-basin bay
scenes.reference_notes: Actual wave-basin image inspected: long row of narrow silver wavemaker paddles with blue vertical trim, exposed top-mounted motors and cables, corrugated metal wall and structural columns behind the array. Only the paddle-side local bay is visible. Photo supports the wavemaker side only. Other WRL flumes have their own different dimensions and are separate facilities; do not assign their widths or lengths to this basin. Visible real waves are not evidence that a static render simulates hydrodynamics.
observed_cues: Repeated silver and blue paddle faces with separate top-mounted motors
Industrial corrugated wall and floor-supported columns behind the array
Local concrete basin edge, without invented complete basin floorplan
